title: Perimeter, Area and the Theorem of Pythagoras
summary: Calculate the perimeter and area of polygons (including parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombi and kites) and circles, using the Theorem of Pythagoras to find missing lengths, and investigate how changing dimensions affects area.

notes.caption: Area formulae for 2D shapes
rows: $h$ is the perpendicular height, not the slanting side

notes.label: Why these formulae work
notes.text: A parallelogram can be cut and rearranged into a rectangle with the same base and height. Two identical trapeziums fit together to make a parallelogram with base $a + b$, so one trapezium is half of $(a + b)h$. A rhombus or kite is half of the rectangle formed around its diagonals.
Using Pythagoras to find missing lengths

Many area and perimeter problems need a length that is not given. Look for a **right-angled triangle** hidden in the shape, for example formed by a height, a diagonal or half of a diagonal, and use $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$.

notes.caption: Isosceles trapezium ABCD with parallel sides AB = 14 cm and DC = 8 cm and height 4 cm. The slanting sides have length s.

notes.title: Worked example 1: a trapezium
notes.problem: For the isosceles trapezium in the diagram, calculate (a) the slant side $s$, (b) the area and (c) the perimeter.
steps: (a) The overhang on each side is $(14 - 8) \div 2 = 3$ cm. In the right-angled triangle: $s^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 25$, so $s = 5$ cm.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a rhombus
notes.problem: A rhombus has diagonals of 10 cm and 24 cm. Calculate its area and the length of each side.
steps: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, giving right-angled triangles with legs $5$ cm and $12$ cm.

notes.title: Worked example 3: an equilateral triangle
notes.problem: Find the height and area of an equilateral triangle with sides of 6 cm.
steps: The height bisects the base, giving a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 6 and base 3.

notes.title: Worked example 4: a path around a garden
notes.problem: A circular garden of radius 10 m is surrounded by a path 2 m wide. Find the area of the path.
steps: Outer circle: radius $12$ m. Inner circle: radius $10$ m.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: The area of the path is **not** $\pi \times 2^2$. Subtract the area of the inner circle from the area of the outer circle.

If every length is multiplied by $k$, the perimeter is multiplied by $k$ and the area by $k^2$. Doubling the radius of a circle multiplies its area by $4$; halving all the sides of a rectangle makes its area a quarter of the original.

items: Parallelogram $bh$; trapezium $\frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$; rhombus or kite $\frac{1}{2}d_1d_2$; circle $\pi r^2$.
Heights are always perpendicular to the base.
Find missing lengths with Pythagoras in hidden right-angled triangles.
Composite shapes: add or subtract areas.
Multiplying lengths by $k$ multiplies area by $k^2$.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. Calculate its area.
A trapezium has parallel sides of 8 cm and 14 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate its area.
A rhombus has diagonals of 10 cm and 24 cm. Calculate its area.
A rhombus has diagonals of 10 cm and 24 cm. Calculate the length of one side.
questions.explanation: Half-diagonals are 5 and 12, at right angles: $\sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$ cm.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives the area of a trapezium with parallel sides $a$ and $b$ and height $h$?
questions.explanation: Half the sum of the parallel sides times the height.

questions.prompt: An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides of 14 cm and 8 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the length of each slanting side.
Calculate the perimeter of the trapezium in the previous question.
Doubling the radius of a circle doubles its area.
questions.explanation: $\pi(2r)^2 = 4\pi r^2$: the area is multiplied by 4.

questions.prompt: Match each shape with its area formula.
questions.explanation: These formulae come from cutting and rearranging shapes into rectangles.

questions.prompt: Calculate the area of a semicircle with a diameter of 10 cm. Use the $\pi$ key and round to two decimal places.
Calculate the height of an equilateral triangle with sides of 6 cm, correct to two decimal places.
A rectangle is 5 cm wide and its diagonal is 13 cm. Calculate its area.

An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides of 14 cm and 8 cm and a perpendicular height of 4 cm.
(a) Calculate the length of each slanting side.  (2)
(b) Calculate the area.  (2)
(c) Calculate the perimeter.  (1)
A circular garden of radius 10 m has a path 2 m wide around it. Calculate the area of the path, correct to two decimal places.

A kite has diagonals of 12 cm and 20 cm. The long diagonal bisects the short one, and is divided by it into parts of 8 cm and 12 cm.
(a) Calculate the area of the kite.  (1)
(b) Calculate the lengths of its sides, correct to two decimal places where necessary.  (3)
questions.memo:
(a) $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 20 = 120\ \text{cm}^2$ ✓ (1)
(b) Half of the short diagonal $= 6$ cm ✓ (1)
Short sides: $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$ cm ✓ (1)
Long sides: $\sqrt{6^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{180} \approx 13{,}42$ cm ✓ (1)
